list / retrieve / partial_update are permission-aware (ORGANIZATIONS bits;
superadmin sees all). create / deactivate / reactivate / destroy are
platform-level and stay superadmin-only via `superadmin_actions`. Every
write is JWT-only through the base API-key gate.

Domain errors (404 not-found, 400 name-conflict, 400 last-active-org) are
raised by the service layer as CustomAPIExeption subclasses and rendered
through the project's `custom_exception_handler` envelope; the view layer
does not catch or translate them.

get.description: Per data type: the organization's chosen days (`null` = instance default), the days actually applied (`*_effective_days`, 0 = keep forever), and the instance `retention_policy` bounding the choices. An organization that never changed its retention returns nulls and null `updated_at` / `updated_by`.

patch.description: Send any subset of `sessions_days`, `conversations_days`, `audit_days`; at least one is required. Each must be one of `retention_policy.<type>.allowed`, `null` to fall back to the instance default, or the value already stored (so a form stays savable after a cap is lowered or a floor raised). `allowed` leaves out values above `max_days` and below `min_days`. Unsent types are left unchanged.

get.description:
Saved audit-search filters of the active org, each private to its author
or shared with the org. list, retrieve, export, bulk_export and copy see
the caller's own presets plus every shared one; a colleague's private
preset 404s there exactly like a preset of another org (bulk_export 400s).
Only the author can update or delete - for those actions get_queryset
narrows to `created_by=request.user`. A copy belongs to whoever made it.
The author may share a preset (`is_shared: true`); un-sharing is rejected
by the serializer.

Gated entirely on AUDIT:read, same as browsing itself - presets are a
convenience over audit data, not audit data itself, so every action
(including create/update/destroy/copy/export/import) maps to READ rather
than the CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE bits DEFAULT_ACTION_MAP would otherwise
require - which were never granted for the `audit` resource type (see
rbac/access/builtin_roles.json: Org Admin only has READ+EXPORT).

Returns a short-lived access token; the refresh token is set as an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie without a Domain: over HTTPS (`DJANGO_REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE=true`) `__Host-auth.refresh` with Secure and Path=/, which also expires a leftover `auth.refresh`; over plain http `auth.refresh` with Path=/api/auth/. `remember_me=true` -> Max-Age = configured refresh lifetime; `remember_me=false` -> Max-Age = 30 minutes. Scoped through the recording's chat -> realtime agent to its agent's org
(mirrors RealtimeAgentChatViewSet's scoping). Recordings whose chat has no
rt_agent (orphaned) are not visible — same accepted trade-off as chat history.

`create` is reachable two ways:
- An authenticated org member (JWT) or a self-issued USER API key, sending
  `X-Organization-Id` as usual — org-scoping is enforced via
  `_assert_parent_in_active_org` exactly like any other child resource.
- The `realtime` service (`voice_call_service._post_recording`),
  authenticated with a `key_type=SYSTEM` API key, once a call ends. That
  caller has no logged-in user/org context and can never supply
  `X-Organization-Id`, and identifies its target purely by the opaque
  `connection_key` — same trust model as `RealtimeAgentChatViewSet.end`.
  For that caller only, `_assert_parent_in_active_org` is skipped (the
  SYSTEM key itself is the authorization check); a self-issued USER key
  still goes through the normal org check, so it cannot attach a
  recording to another org's chat by guessing a `connection_key`.

get.description:
Runs the viewset's secret Use check after validation and before the write.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

post.description: Deletes the requested `ElevenLabsRealtimeConfig` rows the caller may delete, scoped to the active org, and reports every other id instead of failing the request. An id is **not found** when it does not exist, belongs to another org, or is not deletable — the three are indistinguishable by design. An id is **skipped** with `in_use_restricted` when something the caller cannot see references it; usage the caller *can* see does not block. A real delete responds 200 when every id went as requested and 207 when any id was not found or skipped; a dry run always responds 200. `usage` is populated only on a dry run; a real delete returns it empty.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Preview only: report what would be deleted and the usage that blocks the rest, without deleting anything. A preview always responds 200. This is a query parameter: a `dry_run` field in the request body is rejected with 400, as is any body key other than `ids`. A blank or repeated `dry_run` is rejected with 400 too.

DryRunWithABlockedId.summary: Dry run with a blocked id

200.description: A real delete removed every requested id, or a dry run reported what would happen to each id.

207.description: Partial real delete: at least one id was not found or was skipped. The body reports the outcome for every id.

400.description: `ids` is missing, empty, over 500 long, or not a list of positive integers; the body holds a key other than `ids` (`dry_run` included); or `?dry_run` is not a boolean, is blank, or is repeated.

Runs the viewset's secret Use check after validation and before the write.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

post.description: Deletes the requested `EmbeddingConfig` rows the caller may delete, scoped to the active org, and reports every other id instead of failing the request. An id is **not found** when it does not exist, belongs to another org, or is not deletable — the three are indistinguishable by design. An id is **skipped** with `in_use_restricted` when something the caller cannot see references it; usage the caller *can* see does not block. A real delete responds 200 when every id went as requested and 207 when any id was not found or skipped; a dry run always responds 200. `usage` is populated only on a dry run; a real delete returns it empty.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Preview only: report what would be deleted and the usage that blocks the rest, without deleting anything. A preview always responds 200. This is a query parameter: a `dry_run` field in the request body is rejected with 400, as is any body key other than `ids`. A blank or repeated `dry_run` is rejected with 400 too.

DryRunWithABlockedId.summary: Dry run with a blocked id

200.description: A real delete removed every requested id, or a dry run reported what would happen to each id.

207.description: Partial real delete: at least one id was not found or was skipped. The body reports the outcome for every id.

400.description: `ids` is missing, empty, over 500 long, or not a list of positive integers; the body holds a key other than `ids` (`dry_run` included); or `?dry_run` is not a boolean, is blank, or is repeated.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique integer value identifying this gemini realtime config.

An id is **not found** when it does not exist, belongs to another org, or is not deletable — the three are indistinguishable by design. post.description: Creates a new, fully independent graph from the snapshot stored in this version. The new graph is a copy — it does not remain linked to the original. Missing dependencies are stripped from the snapshot and reported in `warnings`. Returns the ID of the newly created graph. A snapshot holding a trigger node (webhook, Telegram, schedule) also requires USE on flows; without it the response is 403 `flow_with_trigger_nodes_requires_use_permission` and nothing is written.

get.description: Read-only: runs the same conversion and dependency filtering as restore and create-graph, then returns the result without persisting anything. Missing dependencies are nulled or dropped and reported in `warnings`, keyed by the version's original node ids. Credential-named fields in the snapshot's graph-level `metadata` are returned as null. A Key-Value node's `key_value_table` is the id of the flow organization's table a restore by the caller would bind (same id and name, else same name), or null when none matches or the caller lacks the node mode's Key-Value table permissions; `key_value_table_name` is the name stored in the version. `node_authorship` maps each snapshot node id to the node's author and last editor with their times, as recorded when the version was saved; a user removed from the organization or deleted is null, and the map is empty for a version saved before node authorship was recorded.

post.description: Restores the target graph to the exact state stored in this version's snapshot. Before applying the snapshot, the service validates that all external dependencies (LLMs, tools, knowledge sources) referenced in the snapshot are still available; any that are missing are stripped and reported in the `warnings` list. If the `backup` query parameter is `true`, the current graph state is saved as a new version before restoring, and its ID is returned in `auto_backup_version_id`. Uses optimistic locking via `save_version` to prevent overwriting concurrent edits. A snapshot holding a trigger node (webhook, Telegram, schedule) also requires USE on flows; without it the response is 403 `flow_with_trigger_nodes_requires_use_permission` and nothing is written.
post.summary: Restore the graph to the state captured in this version, with optional auto-backup before restoring.

Atomically upserts and deletes all nodes/edges for a flow in one request.

- Entity with `id` → update.
- Entity without `id` → create.
- IDs in `deleted` → deleted (validated as belonging to this graph).

FE sends only changed entities. All entities are validated first. If any fail, the entire request is rejected and no DB writes happen.

Requires UPDATE on flows. A non-empty `webhook_trigger_node_list`, `telegram_trigger_node_list` or `schedule_trigger_node_list` (any create or update of a trigger node, including a position-only change) also requires USE on flows; deleting trigger nodes does not.
post.summary: Bulk save all flow nodes and edges

get.description:
Runs the viewset's secret Use check after validation and before the write.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

post.description: Deletes the requested `LLMConfig` rows the caller may delete, scoped to the active org, and reports every other id instead of failing the request. An id is **not found** when it does not exist, belongs to another org, or is not deletable — the three are indistinguishable by design. An id is **skipped** with `in_use_restricted` when something the caller cannot see references it; usage the caller *can* see does not block. A real delete responds 200 when every id went as requested and 207 when any id was not found or skipped; a dry run always responds 200. `usage` is populated only on a dry run; a real delete returns it empty.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Preview only: report what would be deleted and the usage that blocks the rest, without deleting anything. A preview always responds 200. This is a query parameter: a `dry_run` field in the request body is rejected with 400, as is any body key other than `ids`. A blank or repeated `dry_run` is rejected with 400 too.

DryRunWithABlockedId.summary: Dry run with a blocked id

200.description: A real delete removed every requested id, or a dry run reported what would happen to each id.

207.description: Partial real delete: at least one id was not found or was skipped. The body reports the outcome for every id.

400.description: `ids` is missing, empty, over 500 long, or not a list of positive integers; the body holds a key other than `ids` (`dry_run` included); or `?dry_run` is not a boolean, is blank, or is repeated.

Returns raw usage counts for `McpTool` rows visible to the active org, computed against the surfaces attaching the tool. For each tool: `agent_surface_count` (catalog surfaces with a non-null `owner_agent`), `shared_surface_count` (catalog surfaces with a null `owner_agent`), `inline_surface_count` (task-node and agent-node inline surfaces combined) — see the usage-detail endpoint for the per-entry breakdown — and `is_built_in` so the FE can gate orphan-highlighting on `!is_built_in`. `mode="deny"` attachments never count. Does not exclude built-in or orphaned rows itself and does not return reference detail lists — counts only.

Optional `ids` in the request body: a list of numeric ids to scope the response to only those tools, e.g. after the FE paginates its own tools list. Omitted or empty returns all rows for the active org (default, backward-compatible behavior), UNLESS that unscoped result would exceed 50 rows, in which case the request is rejected with a 400 rather than silently truncated — pass explicit `ids` instead. Maximum number of ids is 50.

post.description:
sends a notification email via notification_tool
(channel='email'). Reuses NotificationEmailSender (Django's send_mail /
EMAIL_BACKEND -- the same transport PasswordResetEmailSender uses), NOT a
parallel SMTP client. Requires auth (same DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES /
DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES as every other endpoint), but auth alone
does not prevent abuse: this is driven by notification_tool (LLM output),
so a prompt-injected agent or a leaked API key could otherwise send
unlimited mail to arbitrary external addresses from our domain.
NotifyEmailThrottle caps that per authenticated user.

Plugin service accounts are refused: no resource type governs mail, so a
plugin's declared access could not cap it.

get.description:
Runs the viewset's secret Use check after validation and before the write.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The initial index from which to return the results.

post.description: Deletes the requested `OpenAIRealtimeConfig` rows the caller may delete, scoped to the active org, and reports every other id instead of failing the request. An id is **not found** when it does not exist, belongs to another org, or is not deletable — the three are indistinguishable by design. An id is **skipped** with `in_use_restricted` when something the caller cannot see references it; usage the caller *can* see does not block. A real delete responds 200 when every id went as requested and 207 when any id was not found or skipped; a dry run always responds 200. `usage` is populated only on a dry run; a real delete returns it empty.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Preview only: report what would be deleted and the usage that blocks the rest, without deleting anything. A preview always responds 200. This is a query parameter: a `dry_run` field in the request body is rejected with 400, as is any body key other than `ids`. A blank or repeated `dry_run` is rejected with 400 too.

DryRunWithABlockedId.summary: Dry run with a blocked id

200.description: A real delete removed every requested id, or a dry run reported what would happen to each id.

207.description: Partial real delete: at least one id was not found or was skipped. The body reports the outcome for every id.

400.description: `ids` is missing, empty, over 500 long, or not a list of positive integers; the body holds a key other than `ids` (`dry_run` included); or `?dry_run` is not a boolean, is blank, or is repeated.

For each tool: `agent_surface_count` (catalog surfaces with a non-null `owner_agent`), `shared_surface_count` (catalog surfaces with a null `owner_agent`), `inline_surface_count` (task-node and agent-node inline surfaces combined) — see the usage-detail endpoint for the per-entry breakdown — and `is_built_in` so the FE can gate orphan-highlighting on `!is_built_in`. `mode="deny"` attachments never count. get.description:
Runs the viewset's secret Use check after validation and before the write.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The initial index from which to return the results.

post.description:
Runs the viewset's secret Use check after validation and before the write.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

post.description:
Empty the active organization's recycle bin: every type, a slice per request.

One request per slice instead of one per type: each call purges for a limited time and
says how many items remain, and the client calls again. Each item is its own
transaction, and a failed one is reported, not raised. The bin's most destructive
call, so it has the per-type purges' gates (`purge_permissions`): superadmin only,
never with an API key. Neither an org admin nor a leaked key may wipe a whole
organization's bin.

get.description: Recycle-bin settings. Global, not per organization, so any signed-in user reads them.

post.description:
Test-runs Python code with the provided variables and returns an execution ID to track the run. Send exactly one of `target` or `python_code_id`.

`target` names a code slot of a node in the active organization and runs it the way a real flow run would, including storage access when the node uses storage: the graph's attached files plus a writable folder `test-runs/<type>-<id>/`, reused across test runs of that node.

`python_code_id` runs the bare code without any node settings such as storage.

get.description: Every resource in the active organization that references this secret. A category is present only when it has items, so an unused secret returns an empty list. Flow entries group their secret-using nodes, one entry per code block that uses the secret (`code_field`, null for a node that references the secret by field rather than in code), so a decision table using it in both blocks appears twice with the same node `id`. A node's `id` is its identity — names repeat within a flow — and `node_number` is its display-only badge number, which may be null. `node_type` values are the frontend node-type identifiers. Items in the other categories carry a `type` naming which model they are, because a category can hold several — `llm_configs` folds four and `tools` folds two, and two of them may share a name. Only resources the requesting user has READ permission on are listed; `readable_total` counts those, and `hidden_total` counts the referencing resources withheld, so a secret that is referenced only by resources the caller cannot see reports `readable_total: 0` with a non-zero `hidden_total`.

Within the active organization, omit both. Giving only one of them, or the same organization twice, is a 400. A move across organizations that doesn't fit the destination's storage quota first purges the destination's oldest storage recycle bin entries, just enough of them, and lists them in `recycle_bin_purged` (always empty within one organization); if the whole bin isn't enough, nothing is purged and it's a 413. Returns the limits the streaming upload enforces, so a client can reject an oversize file before sending it. Sizes are in bytes: `max_file_size` caps one plain file (null means unlimited) and `max_archive_size` one compressed archive (always set). `free_bytes` is what the active organization may still upload; it ignores uploads still in flight and does not credit a file the upload would overwrite, and it shrinks as files are added, so read it again before each batch. Files in the recycle bin count against it, but an upload that doesn't fit purges the oldest storage bin entries first when the caller may purge (a user session with FILES:DELETE), so more may fit. A file name is uploaded as an archive (and capped by `max_archive_size`) iff its lower-cased name ends with one of `archive_suffixes` and with none of `document_extensions`; both lists are lower-case, include the leading dot and are sorted. Needs FILES:READ.

A path with nothing live at it contributes nothing, so it is not an error. Flows are those attached to the files and those with a live node whose inline surface is linked to them; agents are those running such a node. For each kind, `used` is always true when a link exists, whatever the caller may read, so nobody destroys links unwarned. `items` lists the distinct entries ordered by name, then id, only when the caller holds READ on that resource type (flows, surfaces or agents) in the active organization; otherwise it is empty. get.description:
Runs the viewset's secret Use check after validation and before the write.

Set `secret_use_check` to a `check_<entity>_write(actor, instance, data)`
function. It is read from the class, so a plain function needs no
`staticmethod`. A viewset that leaves it unset fails on its first write
instead of writing unchecked.

Place this BEFORE `OrgScopedViewSetMixin` / `OrgScopedChildViewSetMixin` /
`OrgScopedHybridViewSetMixin` in the base list: those `perform_create`
overrides call `serializer.save()` without calling `super()`, so a mixin
placed after them would never run.

On a child viewset the parent-in-active-org check runs before the secret
check, so a write under another org's parent is a 404 (cross-org access is
never reported as anything else), not a secret Use 400. The child mixin runs
the same check again afterwards; it is idempotent.

Custom write paths that bypass `perform_create` / `perform_update` (an upsert
branch, an overridden `update`) call `run_secret_use_check` themselves.

Set `secret_use_check_locks_rows` when the check locks rows it reads
(`select_for_update`): the check and the save then run in one transaction, so
the locks hold until the write commits and a concurrent write that takes the
same lock sees this one. It is off by default because the transaction would
also wrap the save's side effects: a TelegramTriggerNode's post_save pushes the
tunnel configs to the webhook service and calls the Telegram API, which must not
run inside an open transaction.

post.description: Sends Telegram `setWebhook` for this node's callback URL even when EpicStaff believes it is already registered, overriding a URL another trigger sharing the bot key holds. A flow save only re-saves changed nodes, so this is how an unchanged node is re-registered. Takes no request body. On success the response is the same object as `GET .../webhook-info/`, read from Telegram after the registration. Configuration problems are checked first, without calling Telegram. Error messages are fixed text; the bot key is never returned.

get.description: Calls Telegram's `getWebhookInfo` for the node's bot key (one attempt, short timeout) and compares the result with this node's own callback URL (`<tunnel>/webhooks/<path>/`). Telegram keeps only the last `setWebhook` URL per bot key, so when several Telegram trigger nodes share a key only one of them receives messages -- `is_match: false` flags a node that is not it. `registered_url` is null when Telegram has no webhook set. `expected_url` is null when the node has no webhook trigger, the trigger is in the recycle bin, has no tunnel provider, uses the localhost provider, or its tunnel URL is not currently available. `is_match` is false when Telegram has no webhook set, and null only when `expected_url` is null (the match cannot be determined); the comparison ignores a trailing slash. `last_error_date` is ISO-8601 UTC. `registration_blocker` is `{code, message}` when this node's configuration makes registration impossible (checked without calling Telegram, by the same rules registration applies), else null. Codes: `bot_key_in_recycle_bin` (then Telegram is not asked, so its fields are null), `no_webhook_trigger`, `webhook_trigger_in_recycle_bin`, `no_tunnel_provider`, `localhost_provider`, `auth_kind_conflict`, `no_telegram_secret`, `invalid_telegram_secret`, `unresolvable_telegram_secret` (`no_bot_key` is answered with the 400 below instead). The bot key is never returned.

post.description: `auth_secret_id` sets/updates this trigger's user-settable auth strategy secret (write-only; the resolved state is echoed back read-only as `auth`: `{kind, secret_id, secret_tail}`, or null when the trigger has no auth; `secret_id` and `secret_tail` are null when the auth row has no secret, e.g. a bare `twilio` reservation. `secret_id` is the id only -- send it back unchanged as `auth_secret_id` to keep the current secret, which needs no secrets:USE permission). `auth_kind` picks which strategy -- `webhook` (`EPICSTAFF_API_KEY`, default if omitted and no auth exists yet) or `telegram` (`X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`; must be 1-256 characters using only `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`, a constraint from Telegram's own Bot API). Setting a `telegram` secret immediately resyncs (re-calls `setWebhook` for) any Telegram trigger nodes already attached to this trigger. A trigger already used by a Twilio channel manages its own auth automatically and rejects `auth_secret_id`. There is no disable toggle: auth is mandatory once a secret is set. If a `telegram` secret update saves successfully but the immediate `setWebhook` resync fails for one or more attached nodes (e.g. tunnel not up yet, Telegram API error), the response still returns 200/201 with the new secret persisted, plus a `telegram_registration_warning` string field describing which node(s) failed and that a retry is needed -- the request is not failed outright since the user's secret was correctly saved.

post.description: Delete the selected items for good, or empty the bin with `all: true`.
Restore the selected items, or the whole bin with `all: true`. Failures are reported per item.

Stream one file straight into storage: the raw body is the file, proxied to object storage in bounded memory. A plain file may be at most DJANGO_MAX_STREAM_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE (default 2gb; none = unlimited). An archive (.zip/.tar*) up to DJANGO_MAX_ARCHIVE_FILE_SIZE is unpacked into a new folder instead. Over either cap: 413 upload_too_large. Everything is also bounded by the organization storage quota: a write that doesn't fit first purges the organization's oldest storage recycle bin entries, just enough of them, and lists them in `recycle_bin_purged`; if the whole bin isn't enough, nothing is purged (413 storage_quota_exceeded). Only a user session (not an API key) holding FILES:DELETE may cause a purge; for anyone else the bin counts as used and the upload gets the 413. The purge commits with the file's row, before object storage completes the upload: if that completion then fails, the request fails but the purged entries stay purged. GET /api/storage/upload-limits/ returns the limits.

The fields are dropped before validation, so their errors cannot reveal which
surface ids exist.

ProfileResponse.description:
GET / PATCH / POST-avatar / POST-tour-complete response for /api/profile/.

Strict superset of UserResponseSerializer: same fields, plus
`active_organization_id`, `active_permissions`, `completed_tours` and
`custom_shortcuts` (the user's own preferences, so they stay off the
admin user directory's UserResponseSerializer). The
`memberships` list is computed in UserProfileService.get_profile — a
normal user's real active memberships, or (for a superadmin) every active
organization with the built-in Superadmin role — so the response shape is
unchanged. `completed_tours` is attached there too and read by a method
field: a user that did not come from get_profile raises AttributeError
instead of silently rendering without the key.

completed_tours.description: Keys of the guided tours the user finished or skipped, sorted.

PythonCode.description:
Adds content_hash as an optional writable field.

content_hash is a computed property on the model (not a DB column), so
ModelSerializer won't include it automatically. get_fields() injects it
so Swagger shows it and clients can pass it. validate() removes it from
validated_data — the view-level ContentHashPreconditionMixin is
responsible for setting instance._expected_hash before save().

venv_id.description: The virtual environment this code runs in. Null runs it in the default one.

secrets.description: Secrets this code is allowed to read, by name. Includes a secret in the recycle bin, which stays linked until it's purged.

execution_timeout.description: Seconds a single run of this code may take before it is killed.

RealtimeChannel.description:
Leave the soft-delete state out of a ModelSerializer, whatever its
`Meta.fields` / `Meta.exclude` say.

Only DeleteService (and restore) write `active`, `soft_deleted_at` and
`soft_delete_batch`. Exposed, they let a client or an import file bin a row
past DeleteService, or break the consistency check (a 500).

NOTE: DRF (3.16) builds the validator for a conditional unique constraint over
several fields, such as a name unique per org among live rows
(`fields=("org", "name"), condition=Q(active=True)`), only when `active` is
among the serializer's fields. With this mixin it never is, so such a clash
surfaces as an IntegrityError instead of a 400: add an explicit validator if
the serializer writes names without deduplicating them first. A conditional
constraint on one field (TwilioChannel's `phone_number`) is unaffected: DRF
always gives that field a UniqueValidator filtered by the condition.

past DeleteService, or break the consistency check (a 500).

NOTE: DRF (3.16) builds the validator for a conditional unique constraint over

(`fields=("org", "name"), condition=Q(active=True)`), only when `active` is

StartNode.description:
Stamp the author on create, never touch it on update, and record real edits.

Every subclass has its resolved `get_fields`, `create` and `update` wrapped, so this
applies whatever the base order; once per outermost call, a last edit is recorded for
a created or changed resource and for the owner it edited (a node's graph). The acting
user comes from `context["request"].user`, falling back to a `created_by` passed
through `serializer.save(created_by=...)`.

The author is only ever set when a row is created: an update drops any `created_by`
it is handed, so a row without an author keeps none.

StorageCopyRequest.description:
Input of a move or copy: within the active organization, or across two of them.

A cross-organization transfer names both organizations and they differ; a transfer
within the active organization names neither. Anything in between is rejected rather
than silently run in the active organization.

source_org_id.description: Source organization ID, for a cross-organization transfer only. Give it together with `destination_org_id`, or omit both.

destination_org_id.description: Destination organization ID, for a cross-organization transfer only. Must differ from `source_org_id`; give both, or omit both.

paths.description: List of file paths to include in the zip

StorageFile.description:
Expose the resource's last edit as read-only `last_edited_by` and `last_edited_at`.

Also renders an exposed `created_by` as the author's user summary (inherited from
`AuthorSummarySerializerMixin`), so a queryset rendered through it should prefetch the
author too unless the serializer does not expose `created_by`.

Both last-edit fields come from one read of `instance.last_edits.all()` per rendered
instance, so a queryset that prefetches `last_edits` with its editor (see
`authorship_prefetches`) adds no query per row. A context with
`OMIT_AUTHORSHIP_CONTEXT_KEY` renders without them.

size.description: File size in bytes, null for folders

created_at.description: When the entry was created; null for tree folders without a row

source_org_id.description: Source organization ID, for a cross-organization transfer only. Give it together with `destination_org_id`, or omit both.

TaskNode.description:
Hides a node's `surface_list` / `inline_surface` from callers without surfaces
READ, and ignores both fields in their writes.

The editor posts back what it was shown, so the hidden (empty) values must not
clear the node's surfaces, nor may such a caller attach surfaces it cannot read.
The fields are dropped before validation, so their errors cannot reveal which
surface ids exist.

applies whatever the base order; once per outermost call, a last edit is recorded for
a created or changed resource and for the owner it edited (a node's graph). The acting
user comes from `context["request"].user`, falling back to a `created_by` passed
through `serializer.save(created_by=...)`.

The author is only ever set when a row is created: an update drops any `created_by`
it is handed, so a row without an author keeps none.

TelegramTriggerNodeField.description:
Adds content_hash as an optional writable field.

content_hash is a computed property on the model (not a DB column), so
ModelSerializer won't include it automatically. get_fields() injects it
so Swagger shows it and clients can pass it. validate() removes it from
validated_data — the view-level ContentHashPreconditionMixin is
responsible for setting instance._expected_hash before save().

TelegramWebhookInfo.description: Read-only shape of `TelegramWebhookStatus` for the node's webhook-info action.

is_match.description: False when Telegram has no webhook set or it points elsewhere; null only when `expected_url` is null.

registration_blocker.description: Why registering this node's webhook cannot work, derived from its configuration without calling Telegram; null when nothing blocks it. Independent of `registered_url`/`is_match`, which still reflect Telegram.

display_name.description: The token user's display name, never empty: the stored name, or one derived from the email when none is stored.

org_ids.description: Org ids the token's user is a member of. Used by internal services (e.g. realtime) to verify the caller owns a given resource's org.

name.description: Optional name for the copied tool. If omitted, the original tool's name is reused with an auto-generated suffix on collision (e.g. "My Tool (1)").

ToolUsageSurfaceEntry.description:
Shared `{id, name, node_id}` shape reused for all three usage-detail
lists — list membership (agent_surface/shared_surface/inline_surface) already
conveys what a `kind` discriminator used to.

`id` is a navigation target, not a unique row key: for `agent_surface`/
`shared_surface` it's the catalog `Surface` id (unique per entry); for
`inline_surface` it's the owning graph's id, which two different nodes in the
same graph can share. `node_id` disambiguates that case — the id of the
`TaskNode`/`AgentNode` the inline attachment lives on — and is always
`null` for `agent_surface`/`shared_surface` entries, which have no node.

TreeNode.description:
Documents the author and last-edit fields of a storage entry, as every API renders them.

Schema-only: the views render storage entries from StorageManager dicts.

created_at.description: When the entry was created; null for tree folders without a row

children.description: Nested TreeNode objects; null for files.

UserResponse.description: Cross-org user payload. Used by /api/admin/users/* endpoints.

UserSummary.description: Read-only public identity of a user: id, display name and avatar URL.

WebhookTriggerFlows.description: Read-only shape of the webhook trigger's flows action.

flow_count.description: How many flows hold a live trigger node on this trigger.

flows.description: The first of those flows by name, then id; empty when the caller cannot read flows.
